neighbours.label: subject pronoun right after a fronted 'what/which <noun>' whose preposition is stranded later (what region they come from, which school you went to); the + pole is the copula before 'from'
fire: Your accent usually gives away what province you come from within a minute.
The form asks which college you went to and nothing else.
Nobody at the party could guess what island she grew up on.
The guide wanted to know which valley they had walked from that morning.
It makes a difference what kind of family you were raised in.
The officer wrote down which district he lived in before the war.
Her cooking tells you exactly what part of Mexico she comes from.
I often wonder which neighbourhood they moved from last year.
quiet: Your accent usually gives you away within a minute of talking.
The form asks for a college degree and nothing else.
Nobody at the party grew up on an island like hers.
The guide had walked up from the valley that same morning.
Being raised in a large family makes a real difference.
The officer lived in the northern district before the war.
Her cooking comes from the southern part of Mexico.
Several families moved away from the neighbourhood last year.

notes: Card: ' who'/' they' peaks, top example 'what region they come from'. Probes: 'which school you went to' 0.70, 'what part of Spain she comes from' 0.47, 'what country they come from' 0.34; plain 'where you come from' 0.07. Weak-to-middling pole; relative ' who' fires only ~0.15-0.24.
